From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>

Subject: BrightGrid vendor setup: required docs for PO issuance

Hi Elena / BrightGrid procurement team,

Thanks for choosing Redwood — excited to get BrightGrid onboarded. To issue the initial PO and route onboarding internally we need the following documentation: 

- Certificate of Insurance (COI) showing General Liability (GL) with limits of at least $1,000,000 per occurrence / $2,000,000 aggregate, Redwood Inference listed as a certificate holder.
- Professional Liability / E&O evidence showing $1,000,000 limit (declarations or binder). If the E&O policy does not permit Additional Insured endorsements, please provide a policy waiver statement or evidence of equivalent coverage.
- Cyber/Privacy Liability evidence (declarations or attestation) with at least $1,000,000 limit.
- Completed vendor onboarding form (attached) and a W-9
- Remittance instructions and the name/email to send invoices to (for the PO).

I've attached the Redwood vendor_onboarding_form.pdf to this email for completion. Once we receive the COI + E&O + W-9 we'll:
1) Validate certificates with Finance/Legal;
2) Create the PO and share the PO number and payment terms;
3) Confirm first invoice processing.

If you need a secure upload, we can provide an SFTP link or our secure intake form — let me know your preference. Please aim to upload/send the docs by EOD next Tuesday (7/7) to avoid delay in PO issuance.

Thanks — appreciate a quick confirmation of receipt.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Vendor Operations | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: vendor_onboarding_form.pdf (1 page, form)

Hi Rachel — thanks for the checklist and the onboarding form (received). Quick questions from our side before we compile everything: 

1) E&O: Our E&O carrier does not add additional insured endorsements for technology professional liability; instead we can provide the E&O declarations page and a letter from the broker confirming coverage limits and effective dates. Will that be acceptable?

2) COI certificate holder: You requested Redwood Inference listed as a certificate holder — do you require Redwood to be added as "additional insured" on the GL as well, or is certificate holder sufficient for PO routing?

We've attached the current GL COI and our W-9. Cyber certificate is being processed and should be back early next week.

Attached: BrightGrid_COI_GL.pdf (COI, 2 pages), BrightGrid_W9.pdf (1 page)

Thanks — happy to schedule a short call if you prefer to walk through any of the items.

Best,

Hi Elena — thanks for the quick reply and for sending the GL COI and W-9. Those look good as initial items. A couple notes: 

- Certificate holder vs. Additional Insured: For our standard PO flow, we require Redwood Inference to be listed as certificate holder on the GL COI. Additional Insured on GL is preferred but not strictly required for smaller integrations — Legal will flag it if we see project-specific exposure. For E&O we can accept the declarations page + broker letter confirming limits if the policy language prevents adding additional insured. Please have the broker include policy number and effective/expiration dates.

- Cyber: appreciate the update — the cyber evidence is required before we can finalize the PO. An interim attestation from your broker indicating coverage is in process is acceptable for conditional PO, but final issuance will wait for the certificate/declarations.

Marcus — when BrightGrid confirms E&O docs + cyber cert, can you confirm the standard net-30 PO template and the contact we should use for remittance so we can route to AP?

Elena — if possible, please upload the final docs to the secure intake link here: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/brightgrid-onboarding-packet. If you prefer SFTP, tell me and I’ll open an account.

Thanks — Rachel
